### 4.2 Who may defer

A `RunContext` has a flag "deferred tool calls enabled". The default is `false`.

- The caller turns it on with `with_deferred_tool_calls(true)`. The host does
  this.
- `handoff_child()` keeps the flag. A handoff child is part of the top-level
  loop, so it can defer.
- `subagent_child()` (workflow agents) and the `AgentAsTool` sub-context set the
  flag to `false`. This replaces the ADR's "depth > 0" rule. Reason:
  `handoff_child()` also adds 1 to `agent_depth`, so a depth rule would deny
  every deferral after a handoff.
- `to_tool_context()` does not project the flag. `AgentAsTool` builds its
  sub-context with `RunContext::new`, so the flag is `false` there. Write a
  regression test in `core/tests/subagent_propagation.rs`. These are the four
  `RunContext` copy sites that every new field must pass through.
- Runners and runtimes that do not support deferral set the flag to `false` on
  the context that they receive, and log one warning when it was `true`:
  `TemporalRunner`, and the axum, actix and agentcore handlers (on the context
  that `ContextProvider::build` returns). MCP and evals build their contexts
  with `RunContext::new`, so the flag is `false` there. One test per runtime.
  The seven build sites (from the SMA-804 session; verify them):
  axum `handlers/runs.rs:220`, actix `handlers/runs.rs:257`, and agentcore
  `invoke.rs:165`, `ws.rs:203`, `agui/sse.rs:147`, `agui/ws.rs:267` and
  `a2a/rpc.rs:519`. Each crate gets one private helper
  `restrict_unsupported_run_features(ctx)`, called directly after each
  `build(..)`. SMA-804 adds its checkpoint clear inside the same helper.

When the flag is `false`, every point that would produce `Defer` produces
`Deny { reason: "approval deferred, but this run cannot defer: {prompt}" }`
instead. The exact text is the builder's call. The `ApprovalHandler` cannot
see the flag (`decide` has no context). Document that a handler that returns
`Defer` gives `Deny` in every context where the flag is off.

A direct `agent.run(ctx, input)` call with the flag on can end with
`RunDeferred`. Only a deferral-aware runner can resume it. Document this.

### 4.3 Authorization with `Defer`

`RunContext::authorize_tool` keeps its stage order: deny rules › guard rules ›
allow rules › mode › policy › approval handler. The loop uses a crate-private
function with a richer result (the decision, the mark, all prompts and the final
args). `authorize_tool` stays the public wrapper and returns
`PermissionDecision`. The rules:

1. **Every ask point asks.** Each guard `Ask` and a policy `AskUser` call the
   handler, as today, also after an earlier ask point of the same call deferred.
   A handler can answer differently per prompt, so a skipped ask point could
   lose a `Deny`.
2. `Allow` from the handler clears that ask point (as today). `Deny` returns
   `Deny`. `Defer` sets the "deferred" mark and records the prompt. The pipeline
   continues.
3. A policy `Defer { prompt }` sets the mark and records the prompt. It needs no
   handler. `AskUser` without a handler is still `Deny`.
4. **Any `Deny` wins**: a later guard `Deny`, mode `Plan` on a non-read-only
   tool, mode `DontAsk`, a policy `Deny`, or a handler `Deny`.
5. **With the mark set, every exit that would return `Allow` or `Replace`
   returns `Defer` instead.** This includes the allow-rule short-circuit, mode
   `Bypass`, mode `AcceptEdits` on a `Write` tool, "no policy installed", and a
   policy `Allow`. Guards exist to beat `Bypass`, so a deferred guard must not
   become an `Allow`.
6. A policy `Replace { args }` with the mark set gives `Defer`. The pending call
   records the replaced args as its effective args, so the approver sees them.
7. The prompt of the result is every distinct recorded prompt, in pipeline
   order, joined with a newline.
8. A call to a tool that the agent does not have is not deferred. It fails as
   today with "unknown tool: {name}". An approval for it would be wasted.

`authorize_tool` returns `Defer` only when the flag (§4.2) is on. Otherwise it
maps the deferral to `Deny`. `execute_tool_call` (`tool_exec.rs`, the durable
path) always maps `Defer` to `Deny`.

The matches without a wildcard in core (`agent.rs` `run_tools_concurrent`,
`tool_exec.rs`, both `ApprovalOutcome` matches in `context.rs`) change with the
new variants. Document in the `ApprovalHandler` docs that one tool call can
produce more than one `decide` call.

### 4.4 The loop: a turn with deferred calls

In `run_tools_concurrent`, a call whose decision is `Defer` is not invoked. It
returns a "deferred" outcome that holds a `PendingToolCall`. The other calls of
the turn run as today, and their results go into the conversation as today.

When a turn has one or more deferred calls:

- The loop does not call the model again.
- The transition moves to `LoopState::NeedsApproval { pending }` and then to
  `NextAction::Terminate`. `pending` keeps its current type
  (`Vec<ToolCallRequest>`). The full data travels in the events.
- On the last allowed turn, the deferral wins over `MaxTurnsExceeded`. The run
  does not call the model again, and a resume gets a new turn budget.
- The events, in this order: the `PermissionDenied` events (the driver yields
  them first, as today), the `ToolOutputItem` of each call that ran, one
  `ApprovalRequested { call_id, tool, args }` per deferred call, then
  `RunDeferred { calls, usage }`. `ApprovalRequested` exists and is never
  emitted today. Change its `args` doc from "arguments the model proposed" to
  "effective arguments".
- The output guardrails do not run. `OnRunComplete` fires once, as on every
  `Terminate`.
- The run span records usage for `RunDeferred`, as for `RunCompleted`, and
  gets an attribute with the number of deferred calls.
- A handoff in the same model response takes precedence over regular calls, as
  today. So a turn never has both a handoff and a deferral.

`TransitionInput::ToolResults { outcomes }` must stay compile-compatible, because
`runtime-temporal`'s driver constructs it. Add a new `TransitionInput` variant
for "results plus deferred calls", or an equivalent. This is the builder's call.
`transition()`'s arm `(NeedsApproval, _) => not_implemented("approval")` goes
away. `NeedsApproval` is now a terminal state.

**Secrets in effective args.** A `PreToolUse` `ReplaceInput` can add values to
the args. Today the effective args are never stored or emitted. Decision (my
call):

- `ToolDeferred` in the session stores the raw effective args, because the
  resume must run with exactly these args.
- `RunDeferred` and `ApprovalRequested` carry the args after redaction with the
  run's `SecretSet`, when output redaction is on. Events reach SSE and AG-UI
  clients, so they must not carry a secret that the run knows.
- `RunResult.stop_reason` comes from the event, so it also has the redacted
  copy. The source of truth for the host is the stored `ToolDeferred`.
- Document that a hook that adds a secret to the args of a call that can defer
  makes the secret persist in the session store.

# Task 5 report: the loop ends a turn that has deferred calls

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (one small change outside the brief, see "Concerns").
Commit: `d80fd157 feat(core): SMA-803 end the run at the turn boundary when a call is deferred`

## What I implemented

- `loop_state.rs`
  - New `TransitionInput::ToolResultsWithDeferrals { outcomes, deferred: Vec<PendingToolCall> }`. The doc says that `deferred` are the event copies, already redacted.
  - New transition arm `(ExecutingTools { calls, usage: prior, .. }, ToolResultsWithDeferrals { .. })`. It is placed before the `ToolResults` arm, and it has no max-turns check. Events: one `ToolOutputItem` per outcome, one `ApprovalRequested { call_id, tool, args }` per deferred call, then `RunDeferred { calls: deferred, usage: *prior }`. `next_state = NeedsApproval { pending }`, where `pending` holds the `calls` entries whose `call_id` is in `deferred`. `next_action = Terminate`.
  - I removed the `(NeedsApproval, _) => not_implemented("approval")` arm. Any input on `NeedsApproval` now goes to the catch-all `invalid transition` arm, which gives `Failed(AgentError::Other)` and `Terminate`.
  - I updated the docs for `NeedsApproval` (it is now terminal), for `NextAction::ExecuteTools`, and for the comment on the `Compacting` arm.
- `agent.rs`
  - A crate-private `enum ConcurrentOutcome { Done(ToolCallOutcome), Deferred(PendingToolCall) }`. `run_tools_concurrent` returns `(Vec<ConcurrentOutcome>, Vec<AgentEvent>)` in call order.
  - `run_tools_concurrent` calls `interceptors.authorize_detailed(.., AskPoints::Ask)`. `Defer { prompt, args }` with a known tool gives `Deferred(PendingToolCall::new(new_deferral_id(), call_id, name, args, prompt, ctx.handoff_path().to_vec()))`, and the tool does not run. `Defer` with an unknown tool gives `Done(Err("unknown tool: {name}"))` and sets the span status to ERROR, the same as the existing unknown-tool path. The old `Defer -> Deny` mapping in the loop is gone, because `authorize_tool_detailed` already does that mapping when the flag is off.
  - `LlmAgent::run` calls `ctx.push_handoff_path(self.name.clone())` once, before the stream starts (`let mut ctx = ctx;`).
  - `ExecuteTools` arm: only `Done` outcomes go into `conversation`. When one or more calls deferred, the arm calls `ctx.deferral_handle().record(raw_pendings)` and makes event copies. The copies use `p.with_args(redact(p.args(), &secrets))` when `ctx.redact_output()` is on, else they are not changed. Then the arm sends `ToolResultsWithDeferrals`. Else it sends `ToolResults` as before.
  - Run span: new field `paigasus.deferred_calls = tracing::field::Empty`. The event loop has a `RunDeferred` arm that records `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` and `paigasus.deferred_calls = calls.len() as i64`.
  - Handoff re-yield: an explicit `RunDeferred { calls, usage }` arm yields `RunDeferred { calls, usage: parent_usage + usage }` and records the span usage and the count.
  - `Terminate` still fires `OnRunComplete` once. Output guardrails run only on `Done`, so they do not run on a deferral.
  - I updated the `redaction_e2e_tests` unit test to unwrap `ConcurrentOutcome::Done`.
- F1 cleanup. I removed the `expect(dead_code)` from all six items, because the non-test code now uses each one:
  `new_deferral_id`, `DeferralSlot::record`, `PendingToolCall::with_args`, `RunContext::push_handoff_path`, `Interceptors::authorize_detailed`, and the `Authorization::Defer.args` field. No `expect(dead_code, ...)` remains in core (`grep -rn 'expect(dead_code' crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src` gives no result).

## Tests

- New `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_calls.rs` has the 8 tests from the brief. It has local helpers: `DeferPolicy` (defers `b` only, or every tool), `RecordingModel` (counts invocations), `InjectSecret` (a `PreToolUse` `ReplaceInput` hook), `CountRunComplete`, and a `tool_arc_all` builder helper.
- `transition_unit.rs`: I replaced `needs_approval_surfaces_not_implemented` with `needs_approval_is_terminal`. I added `tool_results_with_deferrals_emits_approval_then_run_deferred`, which uses turn 15 of 16, so a plain `ToolResults` would trip `MaxTurnsExceeded`.
- `subagent_propagation.rs`: I added `deferral_is_denied_inside_agent_as_tool_sub_run`, which is the regression test for the fourth `RunContext` copy site, and `deferral_is_denied_inside_a_workflow_child`. The inner agent-as-tool model records its requests. The test asserts that the `ToolResult` for `b` in the inner second request starts with `permission denied: approval deferred, but this run cannot defer: `.

### TDD evidence

RED: `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core --test deferred_calls`, run before any source change (`transition_unit.rs` did not compile at that point, because `ToolResultsWithDeferrals` did not exist):

```
test unknown_tool_is_not_deferred ... FAILED
test on_run_complete_fires_once_on_deferral ... FAILED
test deferral_on_the_last_allowed_turn_ends_with_run_deferred ... FAILED
test deferral_in_handoff_child_carries_the_path_and_summed_usage ... FAILED
test deferred_event_args_are_redacted ... FAILED
test turn_with_allowed_and_deferred_call_ends_with_run_deferred ... FAILED
test permission_denied_events_come_first ... FAILED
---- unknown_tool_is_not_deferred stdout ----
  left: "permission denied: approval deferred, but this run cannot defer: policy says wait"
 right: "unknown tool: ghost"
---- deferral_on_the_last_allowed_turn_ends_with_run_deferred stdout ----
run collects: Other(max turns (1) exceeded)
---- (the other five) ----
run collects: Other(no more scripted responses)
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 7 failed
```

These failures are the expected ones. Before the change, the loop turned `Defer` into `Deny` and called the model again. The model had no more scripts, so the run failed (`RunFailed`), or it hit max turns. `flag_off_turns_defer_into_permission_denied` passed, which is correct, because it checks the existing behavior.

The two `subagent_propagation` tests check behavior that Tasks 3 and 4 already made. For this reason they pass before and after the change. To show that they guard the copy sites, I did a mutation check. I set the flag to `true` in the `AgentAsTool` `sub_ctx` (`.with_deferred_tool_calls(true)`) and in `subagent_child()`. Result: `deferral_is_denied_inside_a_workflow_child ... FAILED` and `deferral_is_denied_inside_agent_as_tool_sub_run ... FAILED` (0 passed, 2 failed). Then I put back the original files, and `git diff` shows that no mutation stays.

GREEN: `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core --test deferred_calls --test transition_unit --test subagent_propagation` gives 8 passed, 14 passed, and 8 passed.

Full crate: `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core --no-fail-fast` gives 413 passed and 1 failed. The failed test is `trybuild_ui`, which is known (ruling T1-trybuild). Its `builder_*` cases fail because the local rustc 1.99 renders the diagnostics differently, and no SMA-803 code is in the mismatch. Note: without `--no-fail-fast`, `cargo test` stops at `trybuild_ui`, and the binaries after it (`wire_serde`, `workflow_*`) do not run. I used `--no-fail-fast` so that every binary ran.

Gates: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p paigasus-helikon-core --all-features --no-deps` is clean.

## Files changed

- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs`
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs`
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/control.rs` (F1, and see "Concerns")
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/context.rs` (F1 only: two attributes removed)
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/deferral.rs` (F1 only: three attributes removed)
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_calls.rs` (new)
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/transition_unit.rs`
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/subagent_propagation.rs`

## Self-review

- Event order: the driver yields the `PermissionDenied` events first. The transition events then come in this order: `ToolOutputItem`s, `ApprovalRequested`s, `RunDeferred`. `permission_denied_events_come_first` asserts this order.
- The deferral wins over max turns, because the new arm has no budget check. Both the transition unit test and the `max_turns = 1` loop test assert this.
- The redaction applies only to the event copies. The slot keeps the raw args, and the test asserts both.
- Handoff path: the root pushes its name, `handoff_child` copies the path, and the child pushes its own name. The result is `["triage", "budgeting"]`. The re-yield sums the usage (3 + 4 = 7).
- The `ApprovalRequested.args` doc already says "effective JSON arguments ... redacted", which an earlier task wrote, so I did not change it.
- No version bumps and no CHANGELOG edits.

## Concerns

1. **Change outside the brief (control.rs):** after the change, the loop calls `authorize_detailed`. Only the unit tests in `control.rs` still call `Interceptors::authorize`, so clippy `-D warnings` failed with `dead_code`. I put `#[cfg(test)]` on `Interceptors::authorize` and on its `PermissionDecision` import, and I added a doc line ("Only the unit tests use it."). The other option was an `expect(dead_code)`, but no later task will use this function, so F1 does not apply. A reviewer may prefer to delete the function and change the 20 unit tests to call `authorize_detailed`. That would be a larger change, so I did not do it.
2. The `subagent_propagation` tests cannot show a RED before the change (the reason is above). The mutation check is the evidence that they guard the copy sites.
3. The helpers `DeferPolicy` and `CapturingModel` exist as separate local copies in `deferred_calls.rs` and `subagent_propagation.rs`. I did not add them to `tests/common/mod.rs`, because the brief does not list that file.

## What I implemented

- `loop_state.rs`
  - New `TransitionInput::ToolResultsWithDeferrals { outcomes, deferred: Vec<PendingToolCall> }`. The doc says that `deferred` are the event copies, already redacted.
  - New transition arm `(ExecutingTools { calls, usage: prior, .. }, ToolResultsWithDeferrals { .. })`. It is placed before the `ToolResults` arm, and it has no max-turns check. Events: one `ToolOutputItem` per outcome, one `ApprovalRequested { call_id, tool, args }` per deferred call, then `RunDeferred { calls: deferred, usage: *prior }`. `next_state = NeedsApproval { pending }`, where `pending` holds the `calls` entries whose `call_id` is in `deferred`. `next_action = Terminate`.
  - I removed the `(NeedsApproval, _) => not_implemented("approval")` arm. Any input on `NeedsApproval` now goes to the catch-all `invalid transition` arm, which gives `Failed(AgentError::Other)` and `Terminate`.
  - I updated the docs for `NeedsApproval` (it is now terminal), for `NextAction::ExecuteTools`, and for the comment on the `Compacting` arm.
- `agent.rs`
  - A crate-private `enum ConcurrentOutcome { Done(ToolCallOutcome), Deferred(PendingToolCall) }`. `run_tools_concurrent` returns `(Vec<ConcurrentOutcome>, Vec<AgentEvent>)` in call order.
  - `run_tools_concurrent` calls `interceptors.authorize_detailed(.., AskPoints::Ask)`. `Defer { prompt, args }` with a known tool gives `Deferred(PendingToolCall::new(new_deferral_id(), call_id, name, args, prompt, ctx.handoff_path().to_vec()))`, and the tool does not run. `Defer` with an unknown tool gives `Done(Err("unknown tool: {name}"))` and sets the span status to ERROR, the same as the existing unknown-tool path. The old `Defer -> Deny` mapping in the loop is gone, because `authorize_tool_detailed` already does that mapping when the flag is off.
  - `LlmAgent::run` calls `ctx.push_handoff_path(self.name.clone())` once, before the stream starts (`let mut ctx = ctx;`).
  - `ExecuteTools` arm: only `Done` outcomes go into `conversation`. When one or more calls deferred, the arm calls `ctx.deferral_handle().record(raw_pendings)` and makes event copies. The copies use `p.with_args(redact(p.args(), &secrets))` when `ctx.redact_output()` is on, else they are not changed. Then the arm sends `ToolResultsWithDeferrals`. Else it sends `ToolResults` as before.
  - Run span: new field `paigasus.deferred_calls = tracing::field::Empty`. The event loop has a `RunDeferred` arm that records `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` and `paigasus.deferred_calls = calls.len() as i64`.
  - Handoff re-yield: an explicit `RunDeferred { calls, usage }` arm yields `RunDeferred { calls, usage: parent_usage + usage }` and records the span usage and the count.
  - `Terminate` still fires `OnRunComplete` once. Output guardrails run only on `Done`, so they do not run on a deferral.
  - I updated the `redaction_e2e_tests` unit test to unwrap `ConcurrentOutcome::Done`.
- F1 cleanup. I removed the `expect(dead_code)` from all six items, because the non-test code now uses each one:
  `new_deferral_id`, `DeferralSlot::record`, `PendingToolCall::with_args`, `RunContext::push_handoff_path`, `Interceptors::authorize_detailed`, and the `Authorization::Defer.args` field. No `expect(dead_code, ...)` remains in core (`grep -rn 'expect(dead_code' crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src` gives no result).

- New `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/deferred_calls.rs` has the 8 tests from the brief. It has local helpers: `DeferPolicy` (defers `b` only, or every tool), `RecordingModel` (counts invocations), `InjectSecret` (a `PreToolUse` `ReplaceInput` hook), `CountRunComplete`, and a `tool_arc_all` builder helper.
- `transition_unit.rs`: I replaced `needs_approval_surfaces_not_implemented` with `needs_approval_is_terminal`. I added `tool_results_with_deferrals_emits_approval_then_run_deferred`, which uses turn 15 of 16, so a plain `ToolResults` would trip `MaxTurnsExceeded`.
- `subagent_propagation.rs`: I added `deferral_is_denied_inside_agent_as_tool_sub_run`, which is the regression test for the fourth `RunContext` copy site, and `deferral_is_denied_inside_a_workflow_child`. test deferred_event_args_are_redacted ... FAILED
test turn_with_allowed_and_deferred_call_ends_with_run_deferred ... FAILED
